[dcheck-to-check] Convert DCHECKs in chrome/browser/ [4/25]

As part of effort to harden Chromium's safety, turn DCHECKs
into CHECKs. The converted CHECKs are not fatal until M162.

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tzGQwGG0lJ6K7Ur8wBW6E58CvJc1JQNyiX0ryHe7A5I/edit?usp=sharing

Revert "Clean up NetworkServiceIncreasedPriorityDuringStartup feature flag"

This reverts commit b1b5d936df258af85d0dc2687f5005b9ef51f408.

Reason for revert:
LUCI Bisection has identified this change as the cause of a test failure. See the analysis: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/bisection/test-analysis/b/4821298657099776

Sample build with failed test: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8667833556846125313
Affected test(s):
[://chrome/android\:chrome_public_test_apk!junit:org.chromium.chrome.browser.download:ServicificationDownloadTest#testResumeInterruptedDownloadUsingDownloadOfflineContentProvider](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fchrome%2Fandroid%5C:chrome_public_test_apk%21junit:org.chromium.chrome.browser.download:ServicificationDownloadTest%23testResumeInterruptedDownloadUsingDownloadOfflineContentProvider?q=VHash%3A3cf45aeef473a113)

If this is a false positive, please report it at http://b.corp.google.com/createIssue?component=1199205&description=Analysis%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fci.chromium.org%2Fui%2Fp%2Fchromium%2Fbisection%2Ftest-analysis%2Fb%2F4821298657099776&format=PLAIN&priority=P3&title=Wrongly+blamed+https%3A%2F%2Fchromium-review.googlesource.com%2Fc%2Fchromium%2Fsrc%2F%2B%2F8521143&type=BUG

Original change's description:
> Clean up NetworkServiceIncreasedPriorityDuringStartup feature flag
>
> This feature has launched on Android. Remove the feature flag and
> trigger the startup network thread priority boost explicitly on Android
> via content::BoostNetworkThreadPriorityDuringStartup() from
> ChromeContentBrowserClient::OnNetworkServiceCreated().
>
> Previously, the startup boost was initialized inside
> BoostNetworkThreadPriority::Initialize() on the NetworkService thread,
> gated behind the feature flag and a performance scenario check.
> Hardcoding it there with #if BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID) inadvertently enabled
> the boost on Android WebView and called
> ContentBrowserClient::PostAfterStartupTask() from the NetworkService
> thread, violating AwContentBrowserClient::PostAfterStartupTask()'s UI
> thread check. Moving the trigger to
> ChromeContentBrowserClient::OnNetworkServiceCreated() keeps the behavior
> scoped to Chrome on Android while invoking PostAfterStartupTask() on the
> UI thread, making it safe for WebView to call in the future.
>

🌺 Revert "[TabBottomSheet] Add GlicBottomSheetResizeAndroid fieldtrial config"

This reverts commit 41ebd7f738c8f2c36ac6e67a9feee6c050c14d41.
Culprit: 41ebd7f738c8 - "[TabBottomSheet] Add GlicBottomSheetResizeAndroid fieldtrial config" (refs/heads/main@{#1720297}, https://crrev.com/c/8588996)

Reason for revert: consistently fails android-x64-rel.

Mechanism: Enabling TabBottomSheetResizeWebview in
GlicBottomSheetResizeAndroid fieldtrial_testing_config causes
canResizeWebView() to return true in
TabBottomSheetCoordinator.createSheetContent(), which asserts that
WebViewResizingHelper is non-null. However,
TabBottomSheetManagerTest.setUp() constructs CoBrowseViews with a null
WebViewResizingHelper, causing all 18 tests in TabBottomSheetManagerTest
to fail with AssertionError: WebViewResizingHelper must not be null when
resizing WebView.

TabBottomSheetManagerTest#testBackPressClosesBottomSheet has failed in
3/25 recent builds of android-x64-rel, every attempt in every one of
them. This is not flake: it reproduces on every run, so it blocks the CQ
for every unrelated CL that touches this suite. The regression appears
at refs/heads/main@{#1720297}.

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/try/android-x64-rel/1203567

To run/deflake this test on CQ before relanding, add the following
footer to your CL description:
  Include-Ci-Only-Tests: chromium.android:android-16-x64-rel,chromium.android:android-12l-x64-rel-cq|chrome_public_test_apk

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

Original change's description:
> [TabBottomSheet] Add GlicBottomSheetResizeAndroid fieldtrial config
>
> Add the fieldtrial testing config entry for GlicBottomSheetResizeAndroid
> (enabling TabBottomSheetFullHeight with full_height_ratio=0.95 and
> TabBottomSheetResizeWebview with resizing_placeholder=skeleton,
> resizing_strategy=default) on Android.
>

[initial-letter] Fix block position when size is less than sink

css-inline-3 positions an initial letter whose size is less than its
sink to satisfy its over alignment [1], i.e. its top aligns with the
first line (w3c/csswg-drafts#5329). Blink instead put the box at the end
of the sink-th line, e.g. `initial-letter: 1.5 3` sat on the third line.
Comparing ceil(size) with the sink hid this for sizes like `2.51 3`.

Compare the actual size with the sink, and place such a letter as a
`size >= sink` one without shifting the surrounding text. The initial
letter box still spans its sink, so extend its exclusion to the end of
the sink-th line to keep the same lines wrapping around it.

The change is guarded by the new InitialLetterBlockPositioning runtime
flag.

[1] https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline-3/#initial-letter-block-position

Tests:
- external/wpt/css/css-inline/initial-letter/initial-letter-block-position-over-sunk.html (new)
- external/wpt/css/css-inline/initial-letter/initial-letter-block-position-over-sunk-vrl.html (new)
- external/wpt/css/css-inline/initial-letter/initial-letter-block-position-over-sunk-vlr.html (new)

6cec5416db97e16e04c1b949c900f4da7e5f9bc2 [ diff ] 
ozone/drm: Enable exit-time destructor checks for gbm

The only exit-time destructor left in //ui/ozone/platform/drm:gbm is
the function-local FB_DAMAGE_CLIPS property blob, a process-lifetime
cache in production code. Wrap it in NoDestructor so behaviour doesn't
change, and drop the exemption. The blob is created once and never
updated; crbug.com/572557701 tracks that.

[dcheck-to-check] Convert DCHECKs in chrome/browser/ [1/25]

As part of effort to harden Chromium's safety, turn DCHECKs
into CHECKs. The converted CHECKs are not fatal until M162.

See also:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tzGQwGG0lJ6K7Ur8wBW6E58CvJc1JQNyiX0ryHe7A5I/edit?usp=sharing

This patch is generated by the following script:
https://crrev.com/c/7849874/18/tools/memory/dcheck/replace_dchecks_with_checks.py

PSA:
https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/vd1Qt-egELY/m/badCjDnsDAAJ
LSC (Google internal):
http://goto.google.com/chrome-lsc-dcheck-to-check-conversions

[nastaliq] Add Arabic Nastaliq ("Aran") font preferences and defaults

Add "Aran" (`USCRIPT_ARABIC_NASTALIQ`) to the per-script font family
preferences and `chrome.fontSettings` extension API script enum, and
configure default `standard`, `serif`, and `sans-serif` fonts for Arabic
Nastaliq across Windows, macOS, Linux, and ChromeOS.

These preferences take effect only when `LayoutLocale::
GetScriptForFont()` returns `USCRIPT_ARABIC_NASTALIQ`, which is guarded
by the `NastaliqScript` runtime flag.

blink / extensions: Track auto_resize_constraints separately

Both WebViewImpl::SetIgnoreViewportTagScaleLimits() and
WebViewImpl::ConfigureAutoResizeMode() mutated
user_agent_constraints_.minimum_scale in PageScaleConstraintsSet.

Because WebView::ApplyWebPreferences() unconditionally calls
SetIgnoreViewportTagScaleLimits() on Android whenever preferences are
updated, calling SetIgnoreViewportTagScaleLimits(false) reset
user_agent_constraints_.minimum_scale to -1, overwriting the 1.0f
minimum scale set by ConfigureAutoResizeMode().

We fix this by adding a dedicated auto_resize_constraints_ layer to
PageScaleConstraintsSet, similar to fullscreen_constraints_, and
applying it after user_agent_constraints_ in ComputeConstraintsStack().

We also revert the workaround added in crrev.com/c/8344910.

Move Windows status icon Shell calls off the UI thread

TaskbarCreated recovery synchronously calls Shell_NotifyIcon from the
browser UI thread, which can block while Explorer is unresponsive.

This CL serializes icon registration, updates, recovery and removal on a
MayBlock sequence. Recovery retains the delete-before-add order. Each
request owns its data and retains its icon resources and callback
window. Tray destruction detaches callbacks immediately, and the window
is destroyed on its UI sequence after the last request releases it.

Shutdown does not wait for blocked Shell calls. Pending requests,
including icon removal, may be skipped; a stale icon may remain until
the Shell refreshes it.

Tests cover ordering, UI responsiveness, resource lifetime, weak replies
and shutdown behavior. A manual Explorer restart verified that the icon
and its context menu were restored.

Test: Windows chrome and unit_tests build
Test: 16 tray tests

Mojo Java: Remove try/finally from generated struct decode()

Shrinks Chrome's dex by 13kb.

Every generated struct's decode() wrapped its body in:
  try { ... } finally { decoder0.decreaseStackDepth(); }

javac duplicates the finally body and adds an exception table entry for
every struct. Restoring the stack depth when decoding fails is not
necessary, since the stack depth is tracked per-message, and any
exception thrown while decoding causes the message to be discarded.

This also folds increaseStackDepth() into readAndValidateStructHeader()
to save a call per struct.

[cast] Remove VKEY_BACK from IsBackKey() in CastWebViewDefault

In CastWebViewDefault::PreHandleKeyboardEvent, IsBackKey() previously
included ui::VKEY_BACK alongside ui::VKEY_BROWSER_BACK and
ui::VKEY_ESCAPE. However, ui::VKEY_BACK (0x08) is the Backspace key
(DomCode::BACKSPACE), not the TV remote Back navigation button.

Intercepting ui::VKEY_BACK in PreHandleKeyboardEvent swallows Backspace
key events before they reach the web page and instead dispatches a
synthetic BrowserBack event via back_pressed.js, closing the receiver
application window whenever the page does not call preventDefault() on
BrowserBack.

Remove ui::VKEY_BACK from IsBackKey() so Backspace key presses are
forwarded normally to web contents.

[Media Capture] Fix NPE when the Activity is recreated during the picker

When the Activity is recreated (e.g. on a density or night-mode change)
while the system MediaProjection picker is showing, the restored
MediaCapturePickerHeadlessFragment no longer has a reference to the
pending Delegate, and the picker result callback NPEs.

Keep the pending delegate in a static table keyed by the Activity's task
id, which is stable across recreation and unique per Chrome window. The
entry is removed when the result arrives or the window is closed. A
result with no pending request (process restarted) is dropped, and a
second request from another tab in a window whose picker is already
showing is cancelled up front instead of overwriting the first, so a
picker result can no longer be delivered to a different request.

      picker is up, then pick a tab; sharing starts.

Ash: Move multitask menu to a client-owned widget

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to move Ash widgets off
the deprecated NATIVE_WIDGET_OWNS_WIDGET and WIDGET_OWNS_NATIVE_WIDGET
ownership modes and onto CLIENT_OWNS_WIDGET, the mode views recommends
for all widgets. With it, the code that creates a widget owns it and
decides when it is destroyed. This removes a common source of dangling
pointers and window teardown bugs.

The size button now owns the multitask menu widget. The menu still
closes asynchronously, and the button frees the widget right after the
menu's window goes away.

grit: Stop converting translation text that matches placeholder names

MessageClique.AddTranslation() rebuilt each translation by serializing
it to presentable content and then re-parsing it with a regex built from
the placeholder names. Any translated text that happened to match a
placeholder name (e.g. the word "URL") was thus turned into an extra
placeholder.

E.g. for lv, the translation "vietrādim URL <ph name="URL"/>" was output
as "vietrādim $1 $1" rather than "vietrādim URL $1".

Copy the translation's parts instead of re-parsing. This changes 10
translations (7 message IDs) within chrome/app/generated_resources.grd.

[Omnibox] Only crop the focus scrim for a bottom toolbar

LocationBarFocusScrimHandler set the scrim's bottom margin to the bottom
chin height so the light scrim wouldn't tint the chin
(crbug.com/452336254). That only matters with the toolbar at the bottom,
where the chin is visible below the toolbar while the omnibox is
focused. With the toolbar at the top, the bottom inset is behind the
keyboard, or, with the keyboard hidden, covered by the suggestions list,
which extends through the bottom inset on phones.

With the top toolbar, the crop caused a visible artifact: when
navigating from the omnibox while the keyboard is up, the omnibox stops
consuming the IME inset before the keyboard hides. The scrim's container
then ends at the top of the keyboard, and the crop left an unscrimmed
band right above the keyboard while the scrim faded out.

Only crop the scrim when the toolbar is at the bottom, stopping at the
top of the bottom toolbar. The toolbar is drawn above the scrim, so the
visible result with a bottom toolbar is unchanged.

[css] Move the alias maps into FontFeatureValuesStorage

Parsing an @font-feature-values rule builds six FontFeatureAliases maps
and hands them down through two constructors into
FontFeatureValuesStorage. Each hop took them by value and copied, so the
six HashMaps were deep-copied three times over.

Move at each hop; every caller passes a local it does not use again.

[mac] Re-sync PWA notification permission when app shim becomes active

MacNotificationServiceUN only re-queried the system notification
authorization status at startup, every 10 minutes, and around
notification display / permission requests. This meant that if a user
changed an app's notification permission in System Settings, Chrome
could take up to 10 minutes to notice.

Since the user has to leave the app to change the setting, re-query the
authorization status whenever the app shim's NSApplication becomes
active, by observing NSApplicationDidBecomeActiveNotification inside
MacNotificationServiceUN. The existing de-duplication in
OnGotAuthorizationStatus() ensures the browser is only notified when the
status actually changed, so these extra polls are silent otherwise.

[Omnibox] Defer WebUI suggestion popup creation

Design doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P7h7q6zqhxgPtKhVJBUAU9eb1pawDwK66iQu8CTeRSs/edit?resourcekey=0-nPCcl7S22YgfphQ-H6WV5Q&tab=t.0

When a browser window is built, OmniboxPopupPresenter creates the WebUI
suggestion popup's content in its constructor: a WebContents and its
navigation to the popup page. Like the AI Mode popup, this work
competes with the new window's first frame on the browser UI thread
and in the shared top-chrome renderer.

This CL adds a disabled-by-default feature,
OmniboxWebUIPopupDeferCreation, separate from
OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation so that the two popups can be evaluated
independently. It reuses the deferral support that the parent CL adds
to OmniboxPopupPresenterBase: the presenter overrides
CreateWebUIContent(), and the content is created by whichever of these
comes first:

- A task posted after the browser window's first successful
  presentation. LocationBarView and WebUILocationBar now also pass
  OnBrowserWindowPresented() to the suggestion popup's presenter.
- OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::Show(), when the user types before the
  task runs.

Nothing else reads the suggestion popup content before it is shown:
OmniboxPopupViewWebUI reads it right after Show(), and its selection
methods run only while the popup is open. As with the AI Mode popup, no
fallback timer is needed.

The cost is that typing before the content exists makes the first popup
open wait for the page to load, which is why this popup has its own
feature.

With the feature disabled, creation is unchanged.

The AI Mode popup test for the classic popup's context menu now creates
the classic content first, because that content may be deferred too.

  out/Default/browser_tests --gtest_filter='OmniboxWebUIPopup*'
  and without --enable-features=OmniboxWebUIPopupDeferCreation

[ContextHub] Redesign the Auto Tab Groups view

Replaces the chat-style layout (canvas + chat panel) with the
single-column flow from the UX mockups:
- Landing card with "Check now", a loading skeleton, suggested groups with favicons that can be renamed or dismissed
- "Describe any changes" box whose primary button is "Create groups" or, once a prompt is typed
- "Update" (a follow-up request with chat history)
- Undo for edits made before groups are created
- Clear Groups
- Feedback footer with the privacy disclaimer.

Edits are written back with ReplaceTabGroups so that Create groups
applies what is on screen.

Existing behaviour is preserved: default grouping, follow-up prompts,
confirming and clearing suggestions, switching to a tab, confirmed group
management ("Your tab groups"), ungrouped tabs, and the rating dialog
with its 14-column sheet export. The chat transcript and the
per-response rating are removed; the export keeps its schema with
Source=Canvas.

Adds the first WebUI test suite for the view.

[PDF V2] Cap PdfView zoom bounds to 25% and 500%

Previously, PdfView used its default zoom bounds (0.5x to 25.0x),
allowing pinch-to-zoom and double-tap gestures to zoom beyond the
[25%, 500%] display zoom range supported by the PDF V2 toolbar.

Expose MIN_DISPLAY_ZOOM (0.25f) and MAX_DISPLAY_ZOOM (5.0f) in
PdfToolbarCoordinator and configure PdfView's minimum and maximum
zoom levels in PdfCoordinator#setDefaultZoom relative to the
unclamped 100% baseline zoom. When 25% of the baseline zoom falls
below PdfView.MIN_PERMISSIBLE_ZOOM (0.5f), update PdfView's minZoom
field via reflection so users can still zoom out to 25%.

[Contextual Tasks] Reduce Add tabs menu close delay to 50ms

Previously, the extension Add tabs menu waited 300ms after
pointerleave before closing, causing a noticeable delay when
moving the cursor off the Add tabs row. Since the menu is
anchored directly adjacent to the trigger row, reduce the close
delay in tab_picker_app to 50ms. Also track whether the menu
should remain open and cancel pending close timers on
click/keydown so awaiting setUnbounded does not open the menu
after pointerleave or close it right after activation.

[Reading mode PDFs] Treat combined list marker runs as list items

Line-start text runs that combine an unordered list marker and item text
(e.g. "• Item") are common. Treat these runs as `kListItem` blocks
rather than terminating the list, create a leaf `kListMarker` covering
the marker glyph, and emit the remaining text as static text with visual
bounds adjusted past the marker.

🌺 [Android] Load unit_tests resources.pak directly from APK assets

Previously, unit_tests on Android depended on
//chrome/android:chrome_apk_paks instead of
//chrome/android:chrome_apk_pak_assets and loaded resources.pak from
external storage (DIR_RESOURCE_PAKS_ANDROID/resources.pak) in
ChromeUnitTestSuite::InitializeResourceBundle().

Because multiple host .pak files in runtime_deps flatten to
paks/resources.pak in device_dependencies.DevicePathFor(),
DeviceUtils._GetChangedFiles() can delete paks/resources.pak on reused
DUTs while simultaneously marking it up-to-date. On
android-desktop-17-x64-rel-brya-tests (e.g.
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-desktop-17-x64-rel-brya-tests/1923),
this causes ~160-177 TestingProfile tests per shard to crash in
ntp_tiles::PopularSitesImpl::RegisterProfilePrefs() when loading
IDR_DEFAULT_POPULAR_SITES_JSON, timing out the shard at 60m during
tombstone symbolization.

Package chrome_apk_pak_assets into the unit_tests APK (which also
packages chrome_100_percent.pak and chrome_200_percent.pak into
assets/), load assets/resources.pak directly from APK assets via
ui::LoadMainAndroidPackFile() without a disk fallback, and move
//chrome/browser/diagnostics:unit_tests to !is_android (matching
chrome_main_delegate.cc, as DiagnosticsControllerTest.Diagnostics checks
for a standalone FILE_RESOURCES_PACK file on disk).

Android: Preserve the JNI lookup context for JniZero

The FindClass hook normally tries Chrome's ClassLoader first. When
WebView initializes its own JNI Zero on the same thread, this can
resolve Chrome's org/jni_zero/JniZero instead of the provider's class,
mixing Java and native bindings.

Delegate this exact bootstrap class name directly to the saved JNI
FindClass function. Preserve both its result and any pending exception,
without retrying through Chrome's ClassLoader. Leave all other class
lookups unchanged.

Introduce ml_drift in //third_party/ml_drift

Add the open-sourced ml-drift repository (mirrored from
https://github.com/google-ai-edge/ml-drift) under //third_party/ml_drift
along with its metadata files (README.chromium, OWNERS, LICENSE) and GN
build configuration.

This is the first step in migrating Chromium from the internal copy of
ml_drift in //components/optimization_guide/internal/third_party/odml to
the open-sourced //third_party/ml_drift:
1. This CL introduces //third_party/ml_drift and its GN build targets.
2. Follow-up CL https://crrev.com/c/8545902 builds and statically links
   the LiteRT ML Drift WebGPU accelerator from //third_party/ml_drift
   and //third_party/litert into //services/webnn, replacing the
   dynamically loaded prebuilt libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator library from
   //components/optimization_guide/internal.
3. Subsequent follow-up work will migrate remaining internal consumers
   and remove the duplicate copy in internal odml.

Lookalikes: don't defer non-HTTP(S) navigations for engaged sites

LookalikeUrlNavigationThrottle::WillProcessResponse() defers the
navigation until the engaged sites list has been loaded whenever the
list is stale, which is always the case for the first navigations after
browser startup. However, LookalikeUrlService::CheckUrlForLookalikes()
ignores non-HTTP(S) URLs, so for navigations where neither the first nor
the last URL of the redirect chain is HTTP(S) (the only URLs checked by
PerformChecks()) the wait is pointless.

This notably affects the New Tab Page at startup: in lab traces on a
low-end Mac, the NTP navigation was deferred by ~40-170 ms waiting for
the engaged sites list, delaying its commit and first paint.

Proceed immediately for such navigations instead. The stored
interstitial state is still cleared and interstitial reloads are still
handled before this check, as before.

The new behavior is guarded by the enabled-by-default
kLookalikeSkipEngagedSitesWaitForNonHttp feature, which serves as a
killswitch and allows measuring the impact with a Finch holdback.

Revert "Add MathML support in AnnotatedPageContent"

This reverts commit 445bc609f212f161d9a416a539a8b44312e617fa.

Reason for revert: Causing AIPageContentAgentTest.MathML_RecursionDepth* failures on Win10 Tests x64 (dbg)

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Win10%20Tests%20x64%20(dbg)/56045/overview

Original change's description:
> Add MathML support in AnnotatedPageContent
>
> Previously, MathML elements were treated as generic containers during
> AnnotatedPageContent (APC) extraction, flattening mathematical
> structures and losing formula semantics.
>
> This change extracts <math> elements as kMath nodes with their layout
> display mode (is_block) and sanitized MathML markup (stripped_mathml,
> keeping MathML elements and allowlisted attributes while omitting
> annotations, scripts, hidden or redacted subtrees, and formulas
> exceeding 64 KiB or 128 nesting levels). Descendant layout objects
> continue to be walked so inner text, <mtable> tables, and MathML
> hyperlinks (<a> inside <math>) remain accessible to consumers, while
> nested <math> elements are omitted as separate kMath nodes.
>
> This behavior is gated by AIPageContentIncludeMathML (enabled by
> default) and records the
> OptimizationGuide.AIPageContent.MathSerializedSize histogram.
>

e3cf4f591d270eed7990514b8299d12f095dbdc8 [ diff ] 
[viz] Reject negative frame intervals in FrameIntervalInputs

No client sends a negative ContentFrameIntervalInfo::frame_interval:
compositor scroll entries use zero, video uses zero while its frame
rate is unknown or it isn't playing, and the other content types use
positive intervals. Reject negative values, including
TimeDelta::Min(), when deserializing, so a misbehaving client can't
hand them to Viz, e.g. to its frame interval matchers.

Zero stays valid, and its consumers keep handling it themselves. Very
large intervals are accepted too, up to TimeDelta::Max(): well-behaved
clients can send very long intervals, e.g. for a slow stepped
animation, and not every sender rules out Max().

Also CHECK when serializing, so a bug that produces a negative interval
in a well-behaved client crashes there, with a stack that shows where
it came from, instead of the receiver closing the connection.

Document the rule in the mojom. In the traits fuzz test, generate only
non-negative intervals, and add kSteppedCompositorAnimation to the type
domain.

  ArchivedTabsDialogCoordinatorTest to compute expectedRegularTabCount
  relative to the regular tab count before rescuing archived tabs,
  since opening Settings in a tab adds a regular tab when SettingsInTab
  is enabled.

[Ambient] Match the bubble layout to the mocks

Previously, the title and the rows of the expanded bubble had 16 DIPs of
padding on the sides, and the credential of the collapsed bubble had 12.
Account pictures were shown at 20x20 DIPs.

Now, the bubble follows the UX mocks. The collapsed bubble is laid out
as follows (in DIPs):

  +--------------------------------------------------+
  |                        12                        |
  | 20 Choose your account                     X     |
  |                         8                        |
  |                        10                        |
  | 20 [40x40] 12 Name     16 [Sign in] 12 <>     20 |
  |               idp.example                        |
  |                        14                        |
  +--------------------------------------------------+

The padding on the right of the credential is measured to the expand
icon rather than to the expand button. Passkeys and passwords keep their
20x20 icons.

In the expanded bubble, each row has the same padding (10 DIPs above and
below, 20 on the sides), picture size and spacing between the picture
and the text as the credential in the collapsed bubble, and there are 4
more DIPs below the last row. As in the mocks, the picture is vertically
centered, so it moves down in rows with three lines of text. The rows
show the email and the IdP name in the secondary text color, like the
IdP name in the collapsed bubble.

The size of account pictures is now defined next to FederatedCredential,
so that FedCM crops pictures at the size that the bubble shows them at.

See screenshots before and after the change:
https://issues.chromium.org/u/1/issues/567563304#comment9

[SideUi] Refactor/simplify SideUiObserver events

Replace SideUiObserver#onSideUiSpecsChanged, #onTransitionBegun, and
#onTransitionEnded with #onSideUiSpecsChangeStarted and
#onSideUiSpecsChangeCompleted.
-Previously, these signals were split between static and animated
 updates. #onSideUiSpecsChanged was particularly confusing as it was
 called at the end of a static change and at the start of an animated
 change (via #onTransitionBegun) to adjust views for the new specs.

-Now, both static and animated updates call #onSideUiSpecsChangeStarted
 and #onSideUiSpecsChangeCompleted. Static updates invoke them
 back-to-back, while animated updates invoke them around the
 Transition.

-Most #onSideUiSpecsChanged implementations migrate directly to
 #onSideUiSpecsChangeStarted, so Java View updates are applied right
 after TransitionManager#beginDelayedTransition and picked up by the
 animation.

Adapt observers that could not be migrated one-to-one to maintain
existing behavior.
-CompositorViewHolder#onSideUiSpecsChangeStarted only repositions the
 tab View and disables clipToPadding when animations are not
 suppressed (matching #onTransitionBegun), while composited view
 updates and clipToPadding resets are in #onSideUiSpecsChangeCompleted
 (matching #onSideUiSpecsChanged and #onTransitionEnded).

[SidePanel] Don't resize ThinWebView during live resize (3/4)

Resize side panel content that contains a ThinWebView only once, when
the drag is committed.
-Previously, every live frame of a drag resized the ThinWebView, and
 with it the WebContents, which is too expensive to do on every frame.
-Now, on the first live frame, content containing a ThinWebView is
 pinned at its pre-drag width and aligned to the edge being dragged,
 so it moves with the handle.
-The content is unpinned when the drag is committed, or when it ends
 otherwise, e.g. the panel is closed, its content is replaced, or the
 container is destroyed, so the WebContents is resized once.
-SidePanelResizeManager owns the pinned content together with the
 committed and live widths, so ending a drag always unpins the content.

Revert "[reland][glic] Fix hidden warmup screen height"

This reverts commit c4e9936ac578f0005fbecb9f44889b38e4a36bf7.

Reason for revert: Flakily failing on Win11 Tests x64

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Win11%20Tests%20x64/43094/overview

Original change's description:
> [reland][glic] Fix hidden warmup screen height
>
> This reverts commit 836cb4aef24b96e60698b7058e3b101394a1d73c.
>
> Reason for reland: Fixed timeout in
> GlicVisibilityBrowserTest.ReloadInFloatyRendersFrame on Linux MSan. In
> ReloadAndWait(), the test previously saved a raw WebContents* before
> calling Host::Reload() and waited for web_client_contents() !=
> old_contents. On a cold reload in NoWebview mode, Host::Reload()
> synchronously destroys the old guest WebContents in Hibernate() and
> immediately allocates a new guest WebContents of the same size in
> Awaken(). Under MSan's allocator, the new WebContents was allocated at
> the exact same heap address as the freed one, causing RunUntilNotEqual
> to time out. Fix ReloadAndWait() by tracking destruction of the old
> WebContents via base::WeakPtr<content::WebContents> and waiting for the
> new web_client_contents() to be non-null and ready.
>
> When GlicContentsInitiallyHidden is enabled on Windows,
> RenderWidgetHostViewAura::InitAsChild leaves screen_infos_ at 0x0 when a
> WebContents is created unattached and hidden, causing the guest's
> window.screen.height to be 0 during warmup. Fix this by pulsing
> IncrementCapturerCount(stay_hidden=true) in GlicGuestObserver on the
> top-level WebContents when it is hidden. This triggers
> ShowWithVisibility(kHiddenButPainting) -> UpdateScreenInfo() -> Hide()
> while keeping the WebContents hidden.
>
> Bug: b:513620671, 573268718
> Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter=All/GlicVisibilityBrowserTest.*

[base] Optimize SequenceCheckerImpl::CalledOnValidSequence fast path

Optimize the SequenceCheckerImpl::CalledOnValidSequence() hot path in
dcheck_always_on builds by:
1. Inlining SequenceToken and TaskToken IsValid(), operator==,
   operator!=, and ToInternalValue() (trivial integer comparisons).
2. Caching SequenceToken::GetForCurrentThread() in
   SequenceCheckerImpl::CalledOnValidSequence() instead of reading the
   thread_local variable twice per call.
3. Guarding std::erase_if(locks_, ...) with `if (!locks_.empty())` to
   avoid any work when no locks were held at binding time.

Estimated impact: Saves ~50-90 ms of CPU per browser_test (~1% of total
browser_tests CPU on linux-chromeos-rel).

[base] Optimize TestLauncher test discovery and validation

When launching browser_tests (~48,920 compiled-in tests),
TestLauncher::Init spends ~680 ms (and CollectTests + teardown spend an
additional ~120 ms) copying test metadata and building red-black trees
for all compiled-in tests:
1. TestIdentifier and TestLauncher::TestInfo declare explicit copy
   constructors without move constructors, and GetCompiledInTests(),
   InitTests(), and ProcessAndValidateTests() do not reserve vector
   capacity, causing 16 vector reallocations that deep-copy ~150,000
   std::strings.
2. TestResultsTracker stores all_tests_, disabled_tests_, and
   test_placeholders_ in std::set<std::string>, allocating and freeing
   48,920 red-black tree nodes and performing ~780,000 string
   comparisons on every launcher invocation even when SaveSummaryAsJSON
   is not used.
3. TestLauncher::ProcessAndValidateTests() heap-allocates a temporary
   std::vector<TestInfo> test_sequence for every non-PRE test even when
   pre_tests is empty or has no matching PRE_ test, and CollectTests()
   unconditionally allocates and scans GetPrefixStrippedName() even
   when neither disabled() nor pre_test() is set.

This CL:
- Adds defaulted move constructors and move assignment operators to
  TestIdentifier and TestLauncher::TestInfo, and reserves vector/set
  capacity in GetCompiledInTests(), InitTests(), and
  ProcessAndValidateTests().
- Replaces std::set<std::string> with absl::flat_hash_set<std::string>
  for all_tests_, disabled_tests_, and test_placeholders_ in
  TestResultsTracker, sorting a flat std::vector<std::string_view> only
  when SaveSummaryAsJSON() serializes JSON output.
- Avoids allocating temporary strings/vectors when disabled_ or
  pre_test_ is false.

Estimated impact: ~0.5% to 1.0% of total browser_tests CPU time (~450
ms per TestLauncher invocation) on linux-chromeos-rel.

Retry explicit AAudio input streams on start failure on AL

When we open an AAudio input stream with an explicit device on desktop
Android, `Open()` preempts lower-priority background captures. However,
Chrome waits for a renderer `Record()` IPC before calling `Start()`.
During that gap, a background capture can re-attach to our new Android
input and start first, which causes Android to drop our device ID and
fail `Start()`.

This CL retries a failed explicit-device `Start()` once by closing the
stream and calling `Open()` and `Start()` back-to-back on the audio
thread, behind `AAudioInputRetryOnStartFailure`.

[chromecast] Size bitstream AudioBus to Java buffer capacity

In AudioTrackOutputStream::OnMoreData, the direct ByteBuffer allocated
by Java is sized to 3 * AudioTrack.getMinBufferSize() for the
compressed bitstream format (~24-48 KB for E-AC3), whereas
AudioBus::CalculateMemorySize(params_) computes the uncompressed
float32 planar size (up to 1.18 MB for 6-channel 5.1 E-AC3).

Remove the top-level CHECK_GE against CalculateMemorySize(params_) and
size the bitstream AudioBus::WrapMemory parameters to the aligned
capacity of the Java direct buffer.

[macOS notifications] Stop AppShim service retries after max backoff

Unlike the alert helper process, macOS launches the AppShim process on
demand when a user interacts with an existing notification, and incoming
DisplayNotification or GetDisplayedNotifications calls will also start
the service. Stop scheduling automatic service_restart_timer_ retries
once the restart delay reaches kMaximumServiceRestartTimerDelay (256s)
when MacNotificationProviderFactory::ShouldRetryIndefinitely() is
false (i.e. for NotificationStyle::kAppShim).

Since giving up means notifications may still be on screen, track
whether the service went away without telling us it has no displayed
notifications left. While that is the case, HasNoDisplayedNotifications()
returns false, so GetDisplayedNotifications*() and Close*() relaunch the
service on demand instead of reporting an empty, synchronizable result
(which would cause notification data to be deleted) or silently dropping
close requests. This also fixes the same problem after the user quits
the AppShim (ShutdownType::kUserInitiated).

[macOS notifications] Only reset restart backoff after service responds

Only reset the service restart timer backoff if the notification service
actually responded and remained alive for more than
kServiceRestartTimerResetDelay (10s) since its first response, rather
than measuring from launch time in GetOrCreateService(). This prevents a
never-connecting AppShim that times out after >10s from resetting the
backoff timer to 500ms on every disconnect instead of backing off up to
kMaximumServiceRestartTimerDelay (256s).

Also record Notifications.macOS.{ProcessType}.TimeToFirstResponse on the
first response received from a service connection.

[Push] Shut down Linux D-Bus thread in TearDown

PushMessagingServiceTest and ExtensionsPushMessagingServiceTest own
their own BrowserTaskEnvironment (directly or via
ExtensionServiceTestBase) and do not inherit from
RenderViewHostTestHarness, so they never called
dbus_thread_linux::Shutdown() on Linux. After the shared Linux D-Bus
buses moved onto a dedicated base::Thread("D-Bus thread"), a late D-Bus
reply (ObjectProxy::OnPendingCallIsComplete) initiated during profile
and global feature setup could be posted to the main thread after the
final RunUntilIdle() in ~BrowserTaskEnvironment(), failing
CHECK(MainThreadIsIdle()).

Call dbus_thread_linux::Shutdown() in TearDown() after profile and
global feature teardown so the D-Bus thread is stopped before
~BrowserTaskEnvironment() runs.

Fixed: 569709520
Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter=*PushMessagingServiceTest*

[rust] Use `libs` (not `all_dependent_configs`) for stdlib's system libs

GN reference documentation says that the "use of `all_dependent_configs`
should be avoided when possible".

Before this CL, the system libraries needed by the Rust standard library
were provided by `stdlib_dependent_libs` and
`stdlib_public_dependent_libs` configs.  These configs were applied via
`all_dependent_configs`, and on Windows the libraries were passed as
`ldflags`.  As a result, the libraries were added to the link of every
transitive dependent of `//build/rust/std` - including binaries that do
not contain any Rust code (e.g. `remoting_me2me_host.exe`, which gets
Rust only through `remoting_core.dll`, or most DLLs in a component
build).

The `ldflags` were used, because of a TODO saying that `libs` don't work
on Windows: GN passes `libs` to `rustc` as `-l<name>`, which used to
result in `<name>.lib.lib`.  Today `rustc_wrapper.py` removes the `.lib`
suffix from such arguments, and `rustc`-driven links already get
`-l<name>.lib` from other `libs` (e.g. `-ladvapi32.lib`).

After this CL, the libraries are `libs` (and `frameworks`) of
`source_set`s that `//build/rust/std` depends on.  `libs` set on a
target propagate only until the nearest shared library or executable,
so the libraries are linked only into binaries that contain Rust code.
This is the same approach as used for the prebuilt stdlib rlibs
in https://crrev.com/c/8564239.

Tested by comparing `.ninja` files before and after this CL:
* Linux (with and without `is_component_build`), and a custom
  toolchain with a prebuilt stdlib: no changes in link flags.
* Fuchsia: only the order of `-lfdio` changes.
* Windows (with and without `is_component_build`): every link that
  includes `.rlib`s still gets the libraries (as `libs` for C++-driven
  links or `-l<name>.lib` for `rustc`-driven links).  Links without any
  `.rlib`s no longer get them.
Also cross-built `build/rust/tests:deps` and `base_unittests` for
Windows (with and without `is_component_build`).

Roll third_party/mutter from 48.4 to 51.1

New dependencies and how they're satisfied:
- glycin (mutter 49-50 only, for loading background images): no longer
  used as of 51, so no stand-in is needed.
- xkbregistry (mutter 50+): added to the sysroot in an ancestor CL. The
  bots also need libxkbregistry0 at runtime, which is added to
  install-build-deps.py in https://crrev.com/c/8576638; that must land
  and be provisioned on the bots first. Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 ship
  1.4.0 and 1.6.0 respectively; mutter is built against the sysroot's
  1.0.3 and only uses symbols from libxkbregistry's single V_1.0.0
  symbol version, so any of these work.
- libwayland >= 1.26 (mutter 51): already in tree. (Its README.chromium
  is stale and still says 1.24.0; https://crrev.com/c/8583202 fixes it.)

BUILD.gn:
- Update source lists to match meson's.
- Add the new generated meta-dbus-color-manager and meta-dbus-clipboard
  sources.
- Build meta-selection-source-remote.c unconditionally. Upstream only
  builds it with remote_desktop enabled, but the always-built
  meta-clipboard-session.c uses it.
- Compile the new org.gnome.mutter.experimental gschema, which mutter
  51 requires at startup.
- Add src/mtk/mtk and src/cogl/cogl to the public include dirs, and
  gio/gmodule deps to mtk, matching upstream's include paths and deps.
- Remove a stale copy of gdesktop-enums.h in include/ left over from
  the initial import; clutter now uses the in-tree
  gsettings-desktop-schemas headers like libmutter does.
- Add an xkbregistry pkg_config, drop gdk-pixbuf (no longer used).
- Add -Wno-logical-not-parentheses for clutter, for an upstream
  `!(flags & X) != 0` in clutter-actor.c.
- Use the stable tablet-v2 and staging xdg-session-management protocols
  from //third_party/wayland-protocols instead of mutter's private
  copies (removed upstream).

//third_party/wayland-protocols: add targets for color-representation,
ext-background-effect, pointer-warp, tablet-v2 (stable),
xdg-session-management and xdg-toplevel-tag, which mutter implements.

on_update.sh:
- Drop -Dsm=false and -Dx11=false; the options were removed upstream.
- Provide minimal pkg-config files for dependencies that Chromium
  provides in-tree or via the sysroot (gsettings-desktop-schemas,
  libdisplay-info, libei, colord, udev, xkbcommon, xkbregistry,
  wayland-server/client, wayland-protocols) instead of requiring host
  -dev packages. Using the sysroot's xkbcommon version also keeps
  config.h from depending on the host's
  (HAVE_XKBCOMMON_KANA_COMPOSE_LEDS must be off for the sysroot's
  xkbcommon).
- Wrap the host's wayland-scanner to report the in-tree libwayland
  version (read from third_party/wayland/src/meson.build), as meson
  requires them to match. The generated protocol code isn't used (GN
  generates its own).
- Only build meson's custom targets (the generated sources) instead of
  all of mutter, which would require every dependency on the host.
- Provide a no-op rst2man, since man pages aren't used.

Running the updated script on 48.4 reproduces the checked-in config.h
exactly (other generated files only differ by the newer host
gdbus-codegen dropping G_GNUC_CONST).

Generated files are regenerated with on_update.sh.

Fixes for tests broken by behavior changes in mutter 51:
- ui/ozone/platform/wayland: Honor --force-color-profile, as X11,
  Windows and Mac already do. Mutter 51 describes its sRGB outputs with
  a gamma 2.2 transfer function, so Chromium converted sRGB content for
  display, breaking pixel tests (SnapshotBrowserTest,
  FormControlsBrowserTest, FocusRingBrowserTest) despite browser tests
  forcing an sRGB profile.
- third_party/mutter/chromium/meta-wayland-ui-controls.c: Defer the rest
  of a modified key or mouse button request until the modifier key
  presses have been dispatched. Mutter updates the keymap modifier
  state, which it uses to send wl_keyboard.modifiers, from an idle
  queued by the input thread. When a modifier press and release were
  injected together, both idles ran before the press was dispatched, so
  clients never saw the modifier (e.g. shift-click and ctrl-click
  tests).
- Disable mutter's auto-maximize for tests with a gschema override
  (third_party/mutter/chromium/chromium-tests.gschema.override). Since
  mutter 49, nearly monitor-sized new windows are auto-maximized after
  being mapped instead of before the initial configure. This resized
  high-DPI test browser windows right after their first frame, making
  tests that wait for the initial WebUI paint flaky.

Tested: with --use-mutter, TabDragging DragInSameWindow,
DetachToOwnWindow and DragAll, BookmarkBarViewTest1/2,
BrowserFocusTest.ClickingMovesFocus and TabsRememberFocus, and
KeyboardLockInteractiveBrowserTest.RequestedButNotActive*. The
intermediate 49.5 roll also passed a broader set of 514
interactive_ui_tests (all except
MenuViewDragAndDropTest{InMenuDrag,InMenuDragNoDrop}, which also fail
with 48.4 and with the chromium_48.4 fork). The browser_tests,
interactive_ui_tests and content_browsertests that failed on
linux-wayland-mutter-rel with an earlier patch set now pass locally.

🌺 [WebUI] Load browser_tests.pak from APK assets on Android

On Android, browser_tests.pak is already packaged uncompressed inside
android_browsertests.apk (via //chrome/test:android_browsertests_assets
at assets/browser_tests.pak). However,
WebUIMochaBrowserTest::SetUpOnMainThread() previously loaded
browser_tests.pak from external storage
(DIR_ANDROID_APP_DATA/paks/browser_tests.pak).

On physical Android 17 Brya shards (e.g.
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-desktop-17-x64-rel-brya-tests/1921),
opening /sdcard/chromium_tests_root/paks/browser_tests.pak can fail on
shards, causing all WebUIMochaBrowserTest tests on that shard to fail
with "Failed to load //webui-test/mocha_adapter_simple.js".

Load assets/browser_tests.pak directly from the APK via
base::android::OpenApkAsset().

[Actor] Port TabManagementTool to Android

Previously, TabManagementTool and its ToolRequests
(CreateTabToolRequest, ActivateTabToolRequest, CloseTabToolRequest) were
excluded on Android via skip_android_unmigrated_actor_files because
TabManagementTool and Tool::ValidateBrowserWindow depended on desktop-
only TabStripModel and BrowserWindowInterface::GetTabStripModel().

This change ports Tool::ValidateBrowserWindow, Tool::ValidateWindowId,
and TabManagementTool from TabStripModel/TabStripModelObserver to cross-
platform TabListInterface/TabListInterfaceObserver and
GlobalBrowserCollection, and moves tab_management_tool and
tab_management_tool_request out of skip_android_unmigrated_actor_files
so they build on Android.

The existing desktop tab_management_tool_browsertest.cc is ported to

Fix duplicate background padding in AppMenu width calculation

In AppMenu.show(), bgPadding.left + bgPadding.right was being added
twice when calculating the popup width: 1. int contentWidth = itemWidth
+ bgPadding.left + bgPadding.right; 2. int popupWidth = menuWidth +
bgPadding.left + bgPadding.right; (where menuWidth is clamped from
contentWidth via UiUtils.computeMenuWidth). Because contentView only
subtracts its 9-patch background padding once, adding bgPadding twice
made the inner menu ListView 10dp-12dp wider than the widest item.
Remove the first addition on contentWidth so bgPadding is only added
once when computing popupWidth.

[ReadAloud] Add UMA metrics for Native AI Playback (Overview mode)

Implements missing UMA histograms and enums for AI Playback (Overview
mode) in ReadAloud Native on Clank, addressing remaining TODOs.

The metrics are split into a clear, self-documenting diagnostic
hierarchy:
- Feature / Orchestrator layer (ReadAloudService):
  - ReadAloud.Overview.Outcome: Terminal result of the playback
    preparation (Success, GenerationFailed, ContentParsingFailed).
  - ReadAloud.Overview.TotalDuration: End-to-end user wait time from
    request until audio playback is ready (recorded on success only).

- Remote RPC Subsystem layer (OverviewGenerationBroker):
  - ReadAloud.Overview.ModelExecution.ServerResult: Response outcome
    from the Optimization Guide model execution service (Success, Error,
    Empty).
  - ReadAloud.Overview.ModelExecution.AbortReason: Reasons for
    pre-flight cancellation before dispatching the RPC (NullService,
    EmptyContent).
  - ReadAloud.Overview.ModelExecution.Error: Specific model execution
    error code.

Note: Remote model execution round-trip latency is already measured by
OptimizationGuide.ModelExecution.FetchLatency2.ReadAloudGenerateText.

[chromecast] Keep observing root CastWebContents on inner creation

RuntimeApplicationServiceImpl::InnerContentsCreated() previously called
CastWebContents::Observer::Observe(inner_contents). Because
CastWebContents::Observer is a single-target base::CheckedObserver,
calling Observe(inner_contents) silently detached the observer from the
root CastWebContents.

As a result, any subsequent inner WebContents created by the root
CastWebContents never triggered InnerContentsCreated() or received
SetAppProperties(), leaving its WebContents without
CastPermissionUserData. Remove the Observe(inner_contents) call so
RuntimeApplicationServiceImpl continues observing the root
CastWebContents across all inner contents creations.

033cef0a67a280e7404b9e24c999d3c05c947e82 [ diff ] 
renderer: Fix Use-After-Free in CastBindings

This CL fixes a Use-After-Free vulnerability across CastBinding
subclasses (CastWindowManagerBindings, CastDemoBindings, and
SettingsUiBindings) where C++ methods were bound to V8 JavaScript
objects via gin using base::Unretained(this).

Because the V8 JS function can outlive the CastBinding C++ object (which
is destroyed synchronously when its RenderFrame is detached), invoking
the JS function after frame detachment would result in a use-after-free
and potential renderer sandbox escape.

This fix introduces base::WeakPtrFactory with in-class initialization to
these subclasses and replaces base::Unretained(this) with weak pointers.
It also modifies several CastDemoBindings and CastWindowManagerBindings
methods to take gin::Arguments* args and return void (using
args->Return()) because base::BindRepeating rejects binding WeakPtrs to
methods that return non-void values.

ef5adf65e8dcd6202bbb4d17f91dd1774ff14446 [ diff ] 
[chromecast] Use checked_cast for Starboard media buffer sizes

Potential integer narrowing vulnerabilities exist in
DrmInfoWrapper::Create and StarboardDecoder::PushBufferInternal where a
size_t buffer size is narrowed to a signed int32_t via static_cast or
implicit conversion. If a compromised renderer provides a large media
buffer (2 GiB or larger) with an empty subsamples list, these casts
result in negative values for encrypted_byte_count and buffer_size being
passed to vendor Starboard implementations.

This CL replaces the narrowing casts with base::checked_cast, ensuring
that the process terminates safely (CHECK failure) if a buffer size
exceeds the limits of a signed 32-bit integer, and adds a regression
test for the large buffer overflow scenario without heap allocation
(using dummy external memory).

[actor] [page stability] Defer paint stability timeout until WaitForStable() is called

We have that monitor_start_delay_ (m_s_d_) >= initial_paint_timeout_.
Since we monitor at the beginning of m_s_d_, if no event happens, we
need to avoid timing out and defer doing so until m_s_d_ is duration is
done.

This CL adds Gemini consent check to GetLocalPersonalContextInfo for
code sitting inside of ./components/ to decide whether consent has been

ash: Add MouseShakeToLocateController for Shake to Locate Cursor

Adds the controller that consumes MouseShakeDetector for Shake to Locate
Cursor feature (http://go/shake-to-locate). It observes mouse move event
as an accessibility pre-target event handler.

When a shake starts, the controller saves the current cursor size and
large cursor size, then enlarges the cursor to 64 DIP, or to 128 DIP if
Large Cursor is already on. When the shake ends, it shrinks the cursor
over 100 ms and restores the saved cursor size state.

The controller is only created when `kAccessibilityShakeToLocate` is
enabled, which is now off by default.

Screencast: http://screencast/cast/NDY1MDg3NDc4NDcxMDY1NnwwN2MyYmI0ZC0zYQ

[Contextual Tasks] Log session open duration from ephemeral toolbar button

Adds EntrySource::kEphemeralToolbarButton and records
ContextualTasks.Session.Duration.EphemeralToolbarButton when a side panel
session opened via the ephemeral toolbar button ends (on explicit Close,

record ContextualTasks.SidePanel.UserAction.Close.EphemeralToolbarButton when
the side panel is closed by the user.

[Dictation] Don't allow dictation in password fields

Reworked per discussion: no new renderer signal. Dictation now reads the
existing TextInputState through a small read-only
RenderFrameHost::IsFocusedElementPasswordLike().

It works on Mac, where GetTextInputClient() is null, and uses a node_id
match to avoid the stale-state race. It also covers revealed passwords,
JS-masked inputs, and masked contenteditables. Tests pass on Mac.

[macOS] Distinguish Chrome-launched shims in PollForChromeReady crash

When an app shim's target Chrome instance terminates before the shim
connects, AppShimController::PollForChromeReady() crashes with
"Running chrome instance terminated before connecting." This covers two
quite different situations:
- A shim launched by the user/OS that found a running Chrome via the
  singleton lock, which then went away.
- A shim launched by Chrome itself (kLaunchedByChromeProcessId), where
  that Chrome exited (e.g. due to shutdown) before the shim connected.

Split out the second case into its own LOG(FATAL) so the two can be
told apart in crash reports. Behavior is otherwise unchanged; both
cases still crash so we keep exiting the shim and can track how often
this happens.

[Android] Decouple device command retries from --num-retries

test_runner.py has used --num-retries as the devil default_retries for
adb/device commands since https://codereview.chromium.org/1860693002, so
that passing --num-retries=0 locally would fail fast.

Since crrev.com/c/8398412 lowered --num-retries to 1 for
chrome_public_test_apk (and the _tablet/_desktop variants that share the
binary), adb command retries were also unintentionally lowered from 2 to
1 for those suites.

Add a --device-retries flag that controls device command retries
independently. When unset, it keeps following --num-retries, so behavior
is unchanged for everyone else (including local fail-fast). Set
--device-retries=2 on chrome_public_test_apk to restore the previous adb
retry behavior.

[Extensions] Remove ExtensionActionStorageManager

The ExtensionActionStorageManager was responsible for persisting and
restoring default settings for browser actions in the StateStore.
The browserAction API is deprecated and the action API doesn't use this
persistence.

Remove ExtensionActionStorageManager and clean up associated tests and
test data that only existed to verify browser action persistence.
Convert remaining persistence test, "ValuesDoNotPersist", to use
ActionAPITest directly rather than a parameterized suite.

This does *not* remove any potentially-old values in the state store:
* StateStore is backed by LevelDB, and we don't have the same handy
  "remove old preferences" logic that we do for ExtensionPrefs (and
  Prefs in general).
* Keys are also only loaded on-demand, so this doesn't represent a
  major performance hit.
* Data for this should be very small.
* Nothing has been adding new data to this for >1 year, so any old
  data there has already persisted.

It's not worth the technical complexity to introduce a new handler
for this.

adfea24f2f175677ecb0dde1d4e717c22aff9d3a [ diff ] 
[HLS] Disallow file:// HLS content

pages and scripts loaded from the file:// scheme aren't allowed to read
arbitrary data from other file:// urls (ie, you can't use fetch!), but
HLS was a vector around that, since it allows somewhat programmatic
access to individual bytes of a remote file, which could collectively
allow reading an entire local file.

As a result, the only safe way to stop this is to disable hls content
from loading any file:// urls. It was already impossible to mix file://
and other schemes anyway.

The only real place this was useful was ironically testing, which means
that we have to make some tweaks to the CrossOriginFileDataSourceWrapper
implementation to lie about the URL origin.

[Reading mode PDFs] Fix crash when band-sorting pages with lists

`SortBlockNodesByVerticalBands()` assumed every block is a direct page
child, but `kListItem` blocks are children of their `kList`. Sorting
them dropped blocks from the page and gave list items two parents,
failing `AXTree::Unserialize()`.

Track each `kList` instead of its items in `block_nodes`, so lists move
as one block, and `CHECK` that every block maps to a page child.
Remaining annotations after a trailing list now go in a new paragraph.

[Media] Validate data origin before mutating UrlData or redirecting

Previously, `ResourceMultiBufferDataProvider::DidReceiveResponse()`
called `ValidateDataOrigin()` only after mutating metadata (such as
`set_length()`) on `destination_url_data`, migrating to
`destination_url_data`, and merging cached blocks via
`UrlData::RedirectTo()`. Because the newly created
`destination_url_data` had no `data_origin_` set yet, a same-origin
redirect on a subsequent range request could adopt a different data
origin when answered by a Service Worker, and even without a redirect a
rejected cross-origin response could overwrite `length_` on the shared
`UrlData` in `UrlIndex`.

Split `UrlData::ValidateDataOrigin()` into a read-only
`UrlData::CanAcceptDataFrom(origin, is_cors_cross_origin)` check and a
`UrlData::SetDataOrigin(origin, is_cors_cross_origin)` mutator so that
data origin and CORS cross-origin state are always validated and updated
together:
- Validate `(response_url, is_cors_cross_origin)` against both
  `old_url_data` and `destination_url_data` at the start of
  `DidReceiveResponse()` before mutating metadata, inserting into
  `UrlIndex`, or redirecting, and only set the data origin on
  `destination_url_data` once both checks pass.
- Add `UrlData::CrossOriginFail()` for pre-response security failures in
  `DidFail()` and make `UrlData::set_is_cors_cross_origin()` private.
- Update `UrlIndex::TryInsert()` so that it returns `url_data` rather
  than an incompatible or unmerged `iter->value` when
  `!url_data->Valid()` or `MergeFrom()` fails compatibility validation,
  and `CHECK` that `destination_url_data->CanAcceptDataFrom(...)` holds
  after both `TryInsert()` and `RedirectTo()`.

2690cdaa325248ee62ce39694e653eb7144c78a6 [ diff ] 
Mojo Java: Remove DataHeader statics from generated structs

Shrinks Chrome's dex by 31.7kb.

Generated Java mojom structs each had a VERSION_ARRAY of DataHeader
objects and a DEFAULT_STRUCT_INFO field, which required a <clinit> for
every struct (including every interface method's param / response
struct).

This change passes ints to the Encoder / Decoder instead:
 * Encoding uses getEncoderAtDataOffset(STRUCT_SIZE, STRUCT_VERSION).
 * Single-version structs (the common case) decode with
   readAndValidateStructHeader(STRUCT_SIZE), and so have no static
   state and no <clinit>.
 * Multi-version structs use a flattened int[] of (size, version) pairs.

Validation semantics are unchanged.

[GEiC] Split GlicInstanceMetrics by provider

GlicInstanceMetrics and GlicMetricsSessionManager record their
histograms through a GlicMetricReporter (crrev.com/c/8562081) built
from the instance's profile. histograms.xml declares them as
Glic{GlicProvider}.X (variants "", .Consumer, .Enterprise), so Glic.X
history is unchanged, and each summary states its scope.

Every histogram GlicInstanceMetrics records directly is split, except
(marked "Not split:"): consumer FRE/onboarding (GEiC FRE:
b/571507463), Instance.TurnCount{Profile} (ProfileMetricsService adds
{Profile}), and Instance.Uninterrupted*Duration (recorded by
GlicStateTracker). User actions are unchanged. Absorbs former
crrev.com/c/8464626 and crrev.com/c/8474451.

[Direct Offers] Make OfferNotificationHandler per tab

OfferNotificationHandler no longer keeps any state of its own, so it is
now owned by each tab's ChromePaymentsAutofillClient instead of the
per-profile AutofillOfferManager. The client updates the notification
through its own handler on navigations, when the tab becomes visible and
when the payments data changes.

AutofillOfferManager::UpdateOfferNotificationVisibility() is removed.
The handler's tests move from AutofillOfferManagerTest to a new
OfferNotificationHandlerTest.

No behavior change.

parent
677d02fd7e280ea3c29645fb1e6378e161a1e5b0 [ diff ] 
Implement srcset 'h' descriptor and two-dimensional sizes

Implements the parsing parts of
https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13053 behind the
`SrcsetTwoDimensionalSizes` runtime flag:

- Represent a resolved source size as a `TargetBoxSize` (`width`,
  optional `height`, and `object_fit`), and thread it through
  `SizesAttributeParser`, `HTMLImageElement::SourceSize()`, the preload
  scanner and `BestFitSource*`.
  One-dimensional sizes populate only `width`, so this is a no-op
  refactor for existing behavior.
- Parse the `<positive-integer>h` height descriptor in `srcset` when
  paired with a `w` descriptor, and compute each candidate's source
  concrete width from the `TargetBoxSize` and the candidate's aspect
  ratio when fitting with `contain` or `cover`.
- Parse the explicit `[contain | cover] <length> <length>` source size
  syntax in `sizes`.

Making `sizes="auto"` two-dimensional (using the box height and computed
`object-fit`), and using the `width`/`height` attributes as a default
aspect ratio for candidates without an `h` descriptor, are implemented
in follow-up CLs.

[Actor] Relocate background tab provisioning to ActorKeyedService

This CL decouples background tab provisioning from the Android Service
intent system and moves its initiation directly into ActorKeyedService.

Key changes:
- In ActorKeyedService, notify onPendingTaskAdded when a pending task
  is registered.
- On Android, ActorKeyedService dispatches directly to
  ActorForegroundServiceController.startBackgroundActuation(profile, id).
- In ActorForegroundServiceControllerImpl, preserve foreground tab
  creation/reuse when Chrome is already visible, and delegate to
  ActorBackgroundActuationManager in-process without sending Intents.
- Move EnsureForegroundServiceStarted -> AddPendingTask call-site
  switch from GlicExperimentalTriggeringMessageHandler into this CL to
  keep commits bisect-safe.
- Strip obsolete START_ACTOR_FOREGROUND_SERVICE intent processing and
  background tab provisioning logic from ActorForegroundServiceImpl.
- ActorForegroundServiceImpl is now a lightweight shell hosting the OS
  foreground notification and service binder.

[Omnibox] Remove pre-warming backoffs in PreWarmingRecycledViewPool

Since view pool pre-warming runs during background inflation, remove the
UI-thread staggering/cancellation backoffs (STEP_MILLIS, mHandler,
stopCreatingViews, and mPrewarmedViews) and immediately populate the
recycled view pool on creation. Also remove Prewarmed View Count metric
which is no longer necessary with the removal of the logic for early
dismissal of prewarming.
